workflows.eyebrow: Three assignments for a consulting Work Agent
workflows.title: Move an engagement forward without outsourcing the advice.
workflows.description: Each assignment begins with a client brief and rules you control, returns an inspectable deliverable, and stops before the professional recommendation.

items.title: Turn discovery into a working brief
items.job: Consolidate interviews, documents, constraints, and open questions before the team commits to an approach.
items.output: A client-context brief with open questions and source links.
items.boundary: Consultants validate what the client meant and decide the engagement direction.

items.title: Build an evidence-backed recommendation
items.job: Connect research findings to hypotheses, alternatives, and implications without losing the source trail.
items.output: An evidence matrix, option set, and recommendation narrative.
items.boundary: The consulting team owns assumptions, analysis quality, and final advice.

items.title: Prepare a workshop or executive deck
items.job: Transform approved analysis into a coherent session plan, exhibit list, and editable presentation structure.
items.output: A workshop pack or executive-ready deck outline.
items.boundary: A consultant approves claims, tone, and every client-facing deliverable.

boundaries.title: Let the Work Agent prepare the evidence—not own the recommendation.
boundaries.description: The Work Agent can organize evidence and prepare engagement materials; consultants remain responsible for methodology, interpretation, recommendations, and client commitments.
assists: Client-context briefs, issue maps, and evidence registers

boundaries.note: Floatboat is a general-purpose Work Agent, not a consulting methodology or substitute for accountable advisers. It works inside a persistent workspace; data handling depends on the models, tools, connectors, permissions, and engagement policies selected for that environment.

faq.title: Work Agent questions for consultants and advisory teams
faq.description: Consulting teams need to preserve source trails, adapt to changing client context, and keep recommendations accountable to the people presenting them.

items.question: Is Floatboat a consulting methodology or project-management system?
items.answer: No. Floatboat is a Work Agent for the research, synthesis, drafting, and coordination steps around an engagement. Your team still chooses the methodology, workplan, governance, and system of record.

items.question: Can it produce a client recommendation on its own?
items.answer: It can connect supplied evidence to hypotheses and draft alternatives, but consultants must test assumptions, resolve contradictions, weigh trade-offs, and own the advice presented to a client.

items.question: Can each engagement use its own templates and terminology?
items.answer: Yes. A workspace can begin from the client brief, interview guide, issue tree, exhibit conventions, and review cadence selected for that engagement.

items.question: How do we keep a recommendation tied to evidence?
items.answer: Maintain source links beside claims, distinguish client statements from external evidence, expose unresolved assumptions, and have the workstream owner verify every number and conclusion before it reaches a deck.

items.question: How should confidential client material be handled?
items.answer: Follow the engagement's confidentiality terms and firm policy, separate workspaces where appropriate, grant only necessary access, and review the data handling of every selected model, tool, and connector.

items.question: Will drafts go directly to the client?
items.answer: Not in the recommended setup. Workshop packs, executive summaries, emails, and decks remain editable drafts until the engagement team approves the evidence, language, recipients, and release.

items.question: Where should a consulting team start?
items.answer: Use one completed discovery cycle: provide approved interview notes and background documents, generate a source-linked working brief, and compare it with what the team would normally prepare by hand.
